escalations.title: A resolver gap masked half the evidence for the only genuine defect in this partition
escalations.detail: 063#3[1], 063#3[2], 063#3[3] are UNRESOLVED with reason 'unparseable path segment at [?(@.source.file=='docs/methodology/preregistration/osf/preregistration.md')]'. The resolver cannot handle an equality filter whose right-hand side is a quoted path containing '/' and '.'. Those three values (515/81/100) are the source-file half of the same defective sentence family D adjudicates: era-correct is 520/81/101, so two of the three would have been MISMATCHes. The consequence is not merely a coverage gap — it is that the strongest single signal in P3 (a breakdown reproducing a superseded ledger version across BOTH its dimensions) reached triage at half strength.
escalations.ask: Fix the filter parser for quoted string values containing path separators and dots, then re-run the affected batches. Sweep the whole recompute report for the same UNRESOLVED reason string before GATE 3 — this partition alone surfaced three instances in one claim, so the class is unlikely to be confined to 063.
escalations.affects_partitions: 063#3[1..3] fall outside P3's assignment; whichever partition holds them must be told, or the family will be adjudicated twice on disjoint evidence.

escalations.title: A single estimate band is split across two statuses by tilde placement
escalations.detail: The prose reads '~150–250 commitments'. The instrument scored '~150' as APPROX (061#27[0]) and the bare '250' as MISMATCH (061#27[1]), and the § 4.2 restatement '150–250' as two MISMATCHes (061#42[1], 061#42[2]). One estimate, one band, four rows, two statuses — determined entirely by whether a tilde happened to precede a given numeral. Any aggregate statistic over statuses inherits this artefact.
escalations.ask: Make range detection a first-class extraction feature: a span matching '<a>–<b>' under an estimate framing should emit ONE forecast row carrying both bounds, not two independent count rows. Until then, propagate the approx marker across both ends of any band whose lower bound carries one.

escalations.title: File-era era_check inverts the verdict on at least one P3 row; per-claim blame era is required
escalations.detail: 064-phase2-gate-package#23[2] is era-faithful at its CLAIM era (cfb710752, 2026-07-30 13:39:58, manifest = 326) and era-unfaithful at its FILE era (0bddee998, 22:29:15, manifest = 327, the recovery rerun having landed at 15:31:12 in between). A file-era era_check returns faithful:false and triage would land DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA on a cell that was exact when written and whose divergence was caused by the remedy the same cell prescribes. Ruling 14 already names per-claim era-faithfulness as the deciding axis; this row is the mechanical demonstration of why. The risk is systematic: any document revised after its factual cells were authored — every gate package here — can carry rows in this trap.
escalations.ask: Register as instrument work: era_check should resolve the era commit by `git blame` on the claim's source line range, not by the file's last-modifying commit, and should record which of the two it used so triage can see when they differ. Re-run era_check on all wave-4/5/6 rows whose source document has more than one commit; report the count of rows whose verdict flips.

escalations.title: era_check inherits extraction errors and manufactures era-defects against correct documents
escalations.detail: Two P3 rows carry recorded era_check verdicts of faithful:false that are pure artefacts of a wrong locator. 064-phase2-rulings#7[1]: era_check re-ran a single-pool locator (h9-A-p1, 1,032 features) when the claim's referent is the five-pool union (4,954, confirmed three independent ways including the sentence's own subtype tallies and its 17.2 % proxy). 051#0[0]: era_check re-ran a raw null count (8) when the claim's referent is null-minus-the-by-design-exclusion (7), a definition the document supplies two lines below the claim. In both cases the document is exactly right and the era_check asserts it was wrong at its own era. If these fields reach the ledger unchallenged, the verification programme records two false defects against itself.
escalations.ask: Gate era_check behind locator validation: never emit an era_check for a row whose locator triage has not confirmed, and treat any era_check on a row later reclassified EXTRACTION-DEFECT as automatically void. Sweep prior waves for era_check fields attached to rows whose disposition became EXTRACTION-DEFECT.

escalations.title: One document figure, two extraction encodings, two different 'actual' values
escalations.detail: The 28,682 C3 field-check total is extracted twice from the same document — as 061#29[0] (fields/row carried as live operands from the manifests) and as 062#3[1] (fields/row hard-coded as literals 20/16/16/15/4). At HEAD the first recomputes to 32,123 and the second to 28,727, a 3,396 spread on an identical claim. Both are era-faithful and neither encoding is wrong, but a consumer reading the two rows side by side sees an unexplained contradiction, and any aggregate over abs_error double-counts the claim with incompatible weights.
escalations.ask: Add a duplicate-claim detector keyed on (source_file, value_verbatim, quantity-similarity) that flags multiply-extracted figures, and adopt a house rule for row×field products: operands always live, never literal, so re-extractions of the same figure converge. Note the deeper point for GATE 3 — the literal encoding silently freezes a schema assumption from extraction time, which is precisely the failure mode family A documents in the source material.

escalations.title: The verification corpus is not a stationary target and the instrument assumes it is
escalations.detail: Across the five registries this partition touches, the corpus moved on 2026-07-30, 2026-08-02, and 2026-08-03 — including during the C4 sweep itself. The passes-manifest gained three fields in four days; the analyses-manifest gained three rows; commitments statuses moved twice in one day; flash35 min-text-1of10 run3 oscillated 487→486→486→487→486→487 across six commits. A recompute report is a photograph of a moving subject, and re-running it will keep producing fresh MISMATCHes on documents that were never wrong. 22 of 39 P3 rows (56 %) are this and nothing more.
escalations.ask: Record in the GATE 3 package the recompute report's own corpus commit (the HEAD it was computed against) as a first-class field, so every row is interpretable as 'document era X vs corpus state Y' rather than 'vs now'. Consider freezing a corpus commit for the duration of a sweep, or accepting that per-wave re-execution (ruling 7) must be paired with per-wave era resolution or it will generate divergence faster than triage can clear it.
